tier_rationale: Manufacturer's own product page and datasheet describe a USB-bus-powered, cable-based 2-port KVM switch: 'No software drivers required — simply connect the cables to the computers,' no power adapter needed, and switching is done with a physical remote button on a wired cable. IOGEAR's parent, ATEN Technology (FCC grantee code QLE), files intentional-radiator grants for the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth adapters it sells under the IOGEAR brand, and no such grant exists for the GCS22U, consistent with a device that contains no radio.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes. The switch has no network connection to lose — it only ever speaks USB and VGA to the two computers plugged into it. Pressing the physical button, or the one on the 6-foot remote cable, toggles which machine gets the shared keyboard, mouse, and monitor. There is no app, no account, and no firmware update path of any kind.

repairability.notes: Cables are molded into the unit rather than replaceable; no teardown or spare-parts source was found.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: no software/drivers required, USB bus powered (no power adapter), physical remote-cable switching, OS compatibility list.

FCC grantee index for ATEN Technology, Inc. dba IOGEAR (code QLE): filings are intentional-radiator grants for WiFi modules, Bluetooth dongles, and WLAN adapters sold under the IOGEAR brand. No grant exists for the GCS22U KVM switch, consistent with a device that has no radio.

open_questions: Current retail price varies significantly by seller (IOGEAR's own site lists $79.95; third-party marketplace listings vary); no single authoritative current price was pinned down beyond a band.
IOGEAR/ATEN Technology has no entry in data/vendors.json; no incident was found in this search, but a dedicated audit was not performed.
notes: A manual, mechanical alternative to software-based KVM switching: no drivers of any kind on either connected computer, and the failure mode of unplugging is simply 'pick which cable is live.'
